pages.title: What Nectar does
pages.summary: Plans, seats and usage turned into invoices that show every line’s calculation, and what happens to them after they are issued.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.summary: Run Nectar on your computer, sign in, and enter the business and its tax policy.

pages.title: Prices, customers and subscriptions
pages.summary: Products, versioned prices and meters, customers by their own id, and subscriptions with contract exceptions.

pages.title: Usage
pages.summary: Bring usage in by file or from a pipeline, and check each period's totals before anything is rated.

pages.title: Bill runs and invoices
pages.summary: Draft a month, review its exceptions, approve and finalize numbered invoices whose every line shows its rule.

pages.title: Credits, payments and reminders
pages.summary: Credit notes, payments recorded with their reference, ageing and reminders you send from your own mail.

pages.title: Nectar decline retry table
pages.summary: The versioned decline table, frozen retry limits and reasons that stop collection.

pages.title: Retry timing comparison
pages.summary: Published schedules and known outcomes, measured recovery and the live report's accounting.

pages.title: People, roles and agents
pages.summary: Invite a finance operator or an accountant, and let an agent prepare work that a person approves.

pages.title: Moving in from Stripe Billing
pages.summary: Capture your Stripe records, preview the move, compare in shadow and cut over without billing a period twice.

pages.title: Backup, export and restore
pages.summary: Download invoices, usage and bill runs, and save or restore the whole installation.

pages.title: What Nectar does not do
pages.summary: Payments, sending, tax determination and the other things left out, stated plainly.
